drug_class: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (CTLA-4 blocker / monoclonal antibody)
purpose: Tremelimumab-actl is a cancer-fighting medicine used to treat a type of liver cancer called unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. It is given together with another medicine called durvalumab. It is used when the cancer cannot be removed with surgery.
how_it_works: Your immune system has natural 'brakes' that stop it from being too active. Cancer cells can take advantage of these brakes to hide from your immune system. This medicine works by releasing one of those brakes — a protein called CTLA-4 — so your immune system can recognize and attack the cancer cells more effectively.
common_side_effects: Tiredness, rash or itchy skin, diarrhea, nausea, decreased appetite, stomach pain, constipation, low thyroid levels (which can cause fatigue or weight gain), and changes in liver or kidney lab values. Many patients also notice muscle or joint aches.
warnings: Because this medicine boosts your immune system, it can sometimes cause your immune system to attack healthy organs — this is called an immune-related reaction. This can affect your lungs, liver, intestines, kidneys, hormones, skin, or other organs and can be serious. Tell your doctor right away if you have severe diarrhea, trouble breathing, yellowing of your skin or eyes, severe rash, or unusual pain. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy as it can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period after.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion — meaning it goes directly into a vein — at a cancer clinic or hospital. The typical dose is 300 mg given as a single dose on the first day of treatment, alongside durvalumab. After that, only durvalumab continues on a regular schedule. Your oncology team will determine your exact dosing plan based on your specific situation.
